<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914213_theRebbe_9" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914213_theRebbe_9__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the apparent redundancy in the verse about dwelling in sukkot and the paradoxical requirement that the sukkah be both a permanent dwelling and a temporary structure.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"In sukkot you shall dwell for seven days; every citizen in Israel shall dwell in sukkot."</t>
    <t s="1">And the precise points of our Nesi'im regarding this are known.</t>
    <t s="2">For it is necessary to understand what is the duplication of the matter,</t>
    <t s="3">that after it already commands "in sukkot you shall dwell for seven days"</t>
    <t s="4">[this being a command to all of Israel and to each individual Jew]</t>
    <t s="5">what does it add further by saying "every citizen in Israel shall dwell in sukkot"?</t>
    <t s="6">Also, it is necessary to understand the very essence of the mitzvah of sukkah,</t>
    <t s="7">for seemingly it contains a contradiction.</t>
    <t s="8">For the sitting in the sukkah must be "you shall dwell" as in "you shall reside,"</t>
    <t s="9">for all seven days a person makes his sukkah permanent and his house temporary.</t>
    <t s="10">That just as during the entire year he dwells in his residence in a permanent manner,</t>
    <t s="11">conducting all his affairs there,</t>
    <t s="12">so too must be the manner of his sitting in the sukkah,</t>
    <t s="13">that he should conduct all his affairs in the sukkah,</t>
    <t s="14">and see that the sukkah is his residence and permanent place during these seven days.</t>
    <t s="15">However, together with this,</t>
    <t s="16">the actual construction of the sukkah is a temporary construction.</t>
    <t s="17">For this matter, that the sukkah must be a temporary structure, is a fundamental condition of the mitzvah,</t>
    <t s="18">and therefore a sukkah that is higher than twenty cubits is invalid.</t>
    <t s="19">For one of the reasons for this is that up to twenty cubits, one's dwelling is a temporary dwelling,</t>
    <t s="20">above twenty cubits, one's dwelling is not a temporary dwelling but a permanent dwelling,</t>
    <t s="21">and the sukkah must specifically be a temporary dwelling.</t>
    <t s="22">Nevertheless, for the seven days the sitting in it must be permanent,</t>
    <t s="23">which is seemingly a contradiction.</t>
    <t s="24">Now, in the mitzvah of sukkah there is another unique matter requiring explanation,</t>
    <t s="25">that the mitzvah of sukkah is a positive time-bound commandment,</t>
    <t s="26">and in addition to this, the mitzvah of sukkah is limited by the limitation of time,</t>
    <t s="27">it is also limited by the limitation of place,</t>
    <t s="28">that the place must be a fit place for making the sukkah.</t>
    <t s="29">For one who makes his sukkah under a tree, it is as if he made it inside a house,</t>
    <t s="30">for this is not a fit place for this mitzvah.</t>
    <t s="31">This is unlike other Festivals, where we find a limitation only regarding time, but we do not find that there is also a limitation regarding place.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the connection between the mitzvah of dwelling in the sukkah and the mitzvah of taking the Four Species, and questions why these specific four species were chosen.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">b)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, following the mitzvah of sitting in the sukkah</t>
    <t s="2">("in sukkot you shall dwell")</t>
    <t s="3">comes the mitzvah of taking the Four Species,</t>
    <t s="4">as it is stated,</t>
    <t s="5">"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day, the fruit of a beautiful tree, branches of date palms, and a branch of a thick tree, and willows of the brook," etc.</t>
    <t s="6">[For the mitzvah of sitting in the sukkah is from the first moment at the beginning of the seven days of Sukkot,</t>
    <t s="7">and after this</t>
    <t s="8">(and following it),</t>
    <t s="9">in the morning</t>
    <t s="10">(at dawn,</t>
    <t s="11">and ideally at sunrise)</t>
    <t s="12">the time of obligation for the mitzvah of taking the Four Species begins,</t>
    <t s="13">for its mitzvah is specifically by day].</t>
    <t s="14">From this it is understood that the mitzvah of taking the Four Species has a connection to the matter of the sukkah.</t>
    <t s="15">And particularly according to what is known,</t>
    <t s="16">that the optimal mitzvah is that the taking of the Four Species should specifically be in the sukkah,</t>
    <t s="17">for by this it is further emphasized that there is a connection between the mitzvah of taking the Four Species</t>
    <t s="18">("and you shall take for yourselves")</t>
    <t s="19">and the mitzvah of sukkah</t>
    <t s="20">("in sukkot you shall dwell").</t>
    <t s="21">And it requires explanation,</t>
    <t s="22">what is the connection between these two mitzvot.</t>
    <t s="23">And particularly since seemingly they are separate mitzvot,</t>
    <t s="24">for the mitzvah of sukkah is for seven days,</t>
    <t s="25">unlike the mitzvah of taking the Four Species, the essence of the mitzvah and from the Torah is only on the first day.</t>
    <t s="26">[And further known is the distinction in this between the Temple and the outlying areas,</t>
    <t s="27">as explained in the Gemara,</t>
    <t s="28">the enactment of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.</t>
    <t s="29">From this branch several laws and details of laws that apply even in our time, regarding the distinction between the first day and the six days after it.]</t>
    <t s="30">Now, regarding the Four Species themselves, it is necessary to understand,</t>
    <t s="31">why specifically these four species were chosen.</t>
    <t s="32">For although all of them are of the plant type, nevertheless, from the very beginning of the command it is emphasized that they must specifically be unique species.</t>
    <t s="33">And the species must all be in a manner of beauty,</t>
    <t s="34">as it is stated, "And you shall take for yourselves... the fruit of a beautiful tree," etc.,</t>
    <t s="35">and the Gemara expounded</t>
    <t s="36">that this also applies to the three species that follow</t>
    <t s="37">[even though in the verse "beautiful" is explicitly mentioned only regarding the etrog,</t>
    <t s="38">the first species].</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the mitzvot were given to refine the creations, and that the service of Sukkot is the cause for reaching the service of Shemini Atzeret.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">c)</t>
    <t s="1">Now,</t>
    <t s="2">in addition to the above precise points, it is known from the saying of our Sages,</t>
    <t s="3">that the mitzvot were not given to Israel except to refine the creations through them</t>
    <t s="4">(as explained in many places).</t>
    <t s="5">For in addition to the essence of the mitzvah,</t>
    <t s="6">whose matter is that He sanctified us with His mitzvot and commanded us, and it must be fulfilled in order to fulfill the command and will of the Commander,</t>
    <t s="7">nevertheless, in addition to this, there is in the mitzvah a unique service and effect regarding the service of man in general.</t>
    <t s="8">And so it is regarding the service of Israel on the festival of Sukkot,</t>
    <t s="9">both in the mitzvah of "in sukkot you shall dwell for seven days,"</t>
    <t s="10">and regarding the mitzvah of "and you shall take for yourselves on the first day," etc.,</t>
    <t s="11">and in the Simchat Beit HaShoevah that follows,</t>
    <t s="12">that in all of them there is their matter and their effect in service,</t>
    <t s="13">to refine the creations through them.</t>
    <t s="14">And so it is also regarding the eighth day, Shemini Atzeret.</t>
    <t s="15">And although Shemini is a festival in its own right,</t>
    <t s="16">nevertheless, it is called "the eighth day,"</t>
    <t s="17">which itself indicates its connection to the seven days of Sukkot that precede it.</t>
    <t s="18">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="19">(not only is Shemini Atzeret connected to Sukkot, but moreover)</t>
    <t s="20">that just as simply, in order to reach the eighth, seven days are required beforehand,</t>
    <t s="21">so too is it in their spiritual content of Sukkot and Shemini Atzeret,</t>
    <t s="22">that even though the service of Shemini Atzeret and Simchat Torah comes after</t>
    <t s="23">[i.e., it is higher than]</t>
    <t s="24">the service of the days of Sukkot that precede it,</t>
    <t s="25">nevertheless, the cause and factor for reaching the service of Shemini Atzeret is specifically the service of the seven days that precede it.</t>
    <t s="26">And from this is understood the superiority in the service of Sukkot,</t>
    <t s="27">that it is specifically the cause and factor</t>
    <t s="28">through which one comes to the service, the effluences, and the levels of the matter of Shemini Atzeret.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
